design.decision: Upends who should bid nil: the partner with honors and no low middle cards can now bid nil, while the other partner covers. Every bid becomes a question of which hand to empty.
design.opponent: The nil bid is public; the change happens privately in the nil bidder's hand, so opponents only see [2]s appearing where they expected honors, and they bust the nil with middle cards ([8]-[J]) instead.
design.rationale: A memorable Nil build-around that reverses a basic Spades intuition. Bidding is a fixed moment and the bid is an ordinary choice, so it is not an activated ability, and the change is deterministic. [J]s are left alone on purpose so a nil still carries risk.
design.draftText: When a partner on your team bids nil, every [Q] through [A] they hold becomes a [2]
design.hooks: Bid-gated hand changes: a become/raise effect may carry an 'on' bid trigger; it then resolves deterministically right after bidding (before Hold payoffs are counted), on the hand of each partner the trigger names (each nil bidder for nil:true, both partners otherwise). No randomness: 'every' changes only.
